react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of 10 differentially abundant metabolites (glycine, choline, 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde, adenosine, L-serine, sucrose, L-2-amino-3-oxobutanoic acid, L-cysteine, L-threonine, S-adenosylmethionine) converged on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260 / KEGG:map00260) as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-database ORA ranked this pathway first among 15 results with an FDR of 8.6e-17 and a fold enrichment of 737, driven by 7 input metabolites: glycine, L-serine, L-threonine, L-cysteine, choline, adenosine, and S-adenosylmethionine. MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently confirmed the same KEGG pathway at rank 1 (p=3.3e-07, 5 metabolites) and additionally flagged KEGG:hsa00670 (One carbon pool by folate, p=8.4e-10, 6 metabolites) as the top KEGG hit, consistent with the folate one-carbon unit's role as the methyl-group donor linking glycine-serine interconversion to methionine cycling. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis returned the equivalent MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism as its top hit (p=0.00328, 8 compounds including choline and L-threonine), providing orthogonal empirical-mass confirmation. The convergence across ORA (RaMP + MetaboAnalystR) and network-activity (Mummichog) paradigms strongly implicates disruption of one-carbon unit trafficking between the glycine-serine-threonine node and the methionine/SAM cycle. Driver metabolites glycine (KEGG:C00037) and L-serine (KEGG:C00065) participate as direct substrates in the serine hydroxymethyltransferase reaction (SHMT), while S-adenosylmethionine (KEGG:C00019) and L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097) bridge to cysteine biosynthesis and transsulfuration. The folate-dependent one-carbon pool (hsa00670) is likely engaged because glycine cleavage and serine-to-glycine interconversion both generate or consume 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate.
